Christian Ethos, Vision and Values
'Be a light for all to see.' Matthew 5:16
Our Vision
Our purpose is to work alongside children in their learning to enable and empower them to achieve in all aspects, to aspire to greatness and to respect our world and the people within it.
Due to the ever-changing nature of our school community and strong links with the Armed Forces, we place a huge emphasis on our children and community to be:
Our Aims
We want Colerne Church of England Primary School to provide a vibrant and enriching learning community for learners of all ages to grow and develop in the essential elements for their future life and to make the very most of their unique and personal talents and interests. This is reflected in our School Aims, which are centred on our principle of 'Being a Light for All to See', Matthew 5:16.
Our Values
Our 12 school values have been chosen by the whole school community to reflect our individual setting and needs. They are distinctively Christian, based on our ethos and important, whatever faith or background.
We explore these values during collective worship and in our classrooms, but more importantly, we live and demonstrate them every day and in every interaction.
Our 12 values are linked to key Bible stories and one value is considered in depth each term with the Bible story that supports it.

Collective Worship
Collective Worship at Colerne Church of England Primary School.pdf
Collective Worship at Colerne Church of England Primary School is an extremely important part of our school day. On Mondays, Mr Solomon will lead Collective Worship and this will focus on our term's value or one of the five British Values. On Wednesdays, classes will come together in phase teams to focus on Spirituality and on Thursdays, Mrs Chamberlain or a church visitor will lead Collective Worship based on the Key Bible Story of the term or other Bible stories that support the term's value.

British Values
Promoting Fundamental British Values
In accordance with The Department for Education we aim to actively promote British values in our school to ensure our young people leave school prepared for life in modern Britain. Pupils are encouraged to regard people of all faiths, races and cultures with respect and tolerance and understand that while different people may hold different views about what is ‘right’ and ‘wrong’, all people living in England are subject to its law.
Our school's core Christian values work in harmony with our British Values, and through our work on developing both aspects of children's personal values, we encourage pupils to consider them together.
The Key British Values are:
Democracy
Rule of law
Individual liberty
Mutual respect

Welcome
'Be a light for all to see.' Matthew 5:16
Colerne is a 4-11 Church of England, Voluntary Controlled Primary School built in 1965 standing in its own extensive grounds on the edge of the village. There are at present seven classes some of which are vertically grouped. All classes are of mixed ability with a balance of ages and gender. Wherever possible, children are placed within friendship groups.
We believe that all children can be ‘A light for all to see’ in all aspects of school life. At Colerne Church of England Primary School ALL children are given the opportunity to shine in their learning, lead where they are strong and be willing to accept help from those who can guide them, be it adults or peers. We believe that it is the right of every child to learn in a happy, ordered and harmonious environment. To enable each child to realise their contribution and responsibility as a member of our whole school community to make this school a place in which everyone can feel valued, respected and good about themselves.
We firmly believe a school functions most effectively when a relationship of trust and co‑operation exists between parents and staff. We therefore warmly encourage parents to be actively involved in school life and hope that you will feel able to share your expertise for the benefit of all our children. A thriving Colerne Church of England Primary School PTA exists and everybody is invited to become involved.
“I am very pleased with the stimulating and fun environment in the classroom and throughout the school. The staff know each child well and ensure that each individual’s needs are well catered for. The extra-curricular opportunities are an added bonus on top of an already full and broad curriculum.”
We are a very happy and caring community, in which children feel emotionally secure and their individual needs, talents and interests are genuinely catered for. By providing both the right environment and a wide range of experiences that are stimulating, we excite the natural curiosity that is inside every child and harness it to guide them towards discovery and a love of learning.
We hope that you enjoy your visit to our website, and that you find the information you are looking for. Please feel free to contact Becky Costello our School Business Manager or Mark Solomon our Headteacher with any queries you may have on 01225 742367. Thank you for visiting!
Should you require a paper copy of any of the information on this website, please contact the school office and we would be happy to supply these free of charge

Welcome
At Colerne Church of England Primary School, our aim is to prepare all of our children for the next stage in their lives - wherever or whatever that may be!
My name is Eleanor Lockhart and I am the SENDCo (Special Educational Needs and Disability Coordinator) for our school.
Welcome!
As a school, we pride ourselves on the supportive and inclusive environment that we have created for all of our children. We strive to provide everything we can for all of our children to ensure they have the best experience possible with us. We want them to be best prepared for their next step in life wherever or whenever that may be.
As the SENDCo for our school, my role is work with our children, staff, parents and outside agencies to ensure that we provide everything we can to support any additional needs. There are a wide range of additional needs that children may have but they will broadly fit into the following 4 areas:
We are extremely fortunate to have a dedicated and experienced team of Teaching Assistants that work with children, parents, myself and outside agencies to ensure that any additional needs are being met. Within this team, we have trained ELSA (Emotional Literacy Support Assistants) who are able to support children with their emotional needs. We are also a Thrive School which means that we routinely assess all of our children to ensure that their emotional needs are being supported.
As a school, we work closely with Educational Psychologists, Behaviour Support Teachers, specialist teachers, Speech and Language Therapists and many other outside agencies to ensure that any additional needs are being met.
If you are a prospective parent and would like any further information, please get in touch. If you are a current parent and would like to discuss anything, we have a very open door policy within our school.
My SENDCo working days are Thursday and Friday. I can be contacted via the main office or by email on senco@colerne.wilts.sch.uk

History Club
We are the History Detectives
We meet every Thursday after school to discover more about history.
Keep looking at these pages to see what we discover!
The Great HD Museum
The History Detectives opened the doors to their museum last week and invited all the children in the school as well as staff and parent to see their collections of artefacts. The museum was a great success and child in all year groups enjoyed learning more about the different exhibits and eras. They had the chance to hear about the Ancient Egyptians and write their name in hieroglyphs. The historians also taught the children about WW2, about fossils and bones and much more. The old cameras were a great success and children enjoyed handling them and finding out about how people used to take photos before modern technology.
The History Detectives are now planning what their new projects will be in the New Year. Watch this space for news.
Memorial Walk
Last week the History Detectives had a special visitor. Clair Dimond Mills is a genealogist and local historian and together we went to visit the memorial in the village to look at the names of those that died in the First and Second World Wars. We then went back to the warmth of the classroom to use websites such as Ancestry to search up those that had fallen. We found lots of interesting facts and also about how we can use documents like censuses to find out more about people in the past.
The HD Museum
We have been working hard over the last couple of weeks to put together a museum of artefacts.
There will be displays of fossils and bones, the history of cameras, a mining exhibition, a display of WW2 artefacts and an Egyptian display. Classes will be invited to come and see our museum on Wednesday 23rd and Wednesday 30th November.
Here are some photos of us setting up the exhibits.
Archaeological Dig at Colerne!
The History Detectives are planning on doing an archaeological dig in the school grounds. We know that the Romans had settlements nearby: Roman remains have been found in Euridge and there is evidence of a settlement in the airfield. So we invited Elaine Davis from Chippenham Museum to help us plan our dig.
We started by doing a 'desk search' - we looked at a number of websites to see what the land was used for in the past. We discovered that part of the school grounds used to be a quarry so we can't dig there. The rest of it was arable land. After looking at some examples of Roman artefacts - the type of thing that we might find - we walked the grounds to decide on where we could do our dig. This will have to wait until the spring as the ground is too wet and hard in the winter. Keep checking back for more news about or dig!

We went to the Corsham Football tournament and played against 4 teams: Box, Neston, Corsham Primary and Corsham Regis. Some matches were challenging but it turned out great in the end, we won our first 2 matches and then drew our third and won the last. When we sat down to see who came 1st, we felt confident that we would win. Our team was very good at being fair as well as supporting others. It was a very nice time and everybody felt glad they went. – Written by George and George

Governors/Governance
Our School Governing Body
Governors are a voluntary body of people who guide and support the strategic direction of the school. They are members of the school team and their contribution to the running of the school is highly valued.
School Governing Body
The instrument of government states that the Governing Board shall consist of:
3 parent Governors
1 local authority Governor
1 staff Governor
3 Foundation Governors
3 co-opted Governors
The role of the governing body is a strategic one, its key functions are to:
All communications should be addressed to the Clerk to the Governors, Stephanie Cuthbertson, contact email stephanie.cuthbertson@colerne.wilts.sch.uk
Midas Gordon-Farleigh
Chair of Governors/Foundation Governor
Local Authority Governor
Ex-officio - Headteacher
The governors believe it is important that boards reflect the diversity of the school communities they serve. Diverse boards promote inclusive school environments and provide diverse role models for staff and young people.
The governors are currently collecting data on the diversity of the board, including data on age, gender, and ethnicity. They will use that data to inform their recruitment and training needs and ensure there is always a diverse range of perspectives around the table to support robust decision making.
Due to our relatively small governing board, we will not publish this diversity data online as individual governors could be identified and we have a legal obligation to protect their personal data.

Safeguarding Children
Security
The safety of our children is paramount. The school operates a controlled access system with some doors allowing exit only. All children and staff take part in regular emergency drills.
Parents requiring access to the school should use the main entrance. An intercom is provided for use when the office is unmanned.
We also appreciate the support of our parents and local community in the form of a neighbourhood watch.
Complaints and Concerns
If, as a parent, you have a concern regarding your child’s academic progress or personal well-being, then please arrange to speak to his or her class teacher as soon as possible.
Should the concern or complaint be associated with the curriculum or a whole school issue, then please contact the Headteacher who will endeavour to resolve the problem immediately. If, following this course of action, the situation remains unresolved, then there is a formal complaints procedure, details of which are available from the School Office.
School Rules
As we aim to develop a responsible attitude towards each other and to our environment, school rules are kept to a minimum.
They are based on safe and thoughtful actions and behaviour, with a genuine consideration and respect for others and our school.
All children, parents and staff sign up to our Home School Agreement.

Curriculum
Colerne Church of England Primary School Curriculum
The national curriculum (2014) is intended to, “provide pupils with an introduction to the essential knowledge that they need to be educated citizens”. A link to the national curriculum can be found at the bottom of this text. However the national curriculum is just one element of the education of our children in Colerne Church of England Primary School; it is up to us to decide which other enriching experiences we feel should be woven into the curriculum content and how we teach it, thereby enabling all children to make the very best of their learning opportunities. At Colerne Church of England Primary School we believe in providing every possible opportunity to develop the full potential of all learners. Our aim is that all learners will Achieve, Aspire and Respect Together, and in so doing, they will embody our Bible quote from Matthew 5:16 'Be a Light for all To See'.
Through our curriculum we strive to promote a love of learning in all our children, a belief in themselves and what they are capable of achieving and a recognition of Christian and British values. We light up for them a sense of imagination, an appreciation for creativity and a passion to innovate – in short to become someone more than they or their family ever believed they could become.
At Colerne Church of England Primary School all class teachers are responsible for providing a curriculum that is suitable for all pupils in the class, including those with Special Educational Needs or Disabilities (SEND) with support from the SENCo. We have high expectations for all pupils and are committed to ensuring our curriculum complies with the Equality Act 2010 and the Special Educational Needs and Disability Regulations 2014. Our inclusion statement emphasises the importance of providing an inclusive learning environment for all pupils including those with SEND. Additional information on this can be found in our Special Educational Needs Policy and Equality Scheme Policy.
We welcome suggestions from our parents regarding our curriculum. If you have any suggestions, please don't hesitate to get in touch.
